description:
The Micro Finance Scheme under the Gujarat National Dairy Development and Training Centre (GNDTDC) was launched on 1st April 2016. 

This scheme aims to provide financial assistance to dairy farmers and women self-help groups in rural areas. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to enhance the income of dairy farmers by providing them with access to affordable credit. 

The scheme specifically targets small and marginal farmers who require financial support to improve their dairy operations. 

The GNDTDC aims to empower women by promoting their participation in dairy farming through self-help groups. 

The scheme intends to provide loans up to INR 1 lakh per beneficiary. 

The interest rate on these loans is set at a competitive rate of 7 percent per annum. 

The repayment period for these loans is typically 3 years. 

The scheme also aims to provide training and capacity-building programs for beneficiaries to improve their dairy farming practices. 

The GNDTDC has set a target of disbursing loans to at least 10,000 beneficiaries in the first year of the scheme. 

The scheme also aims to create a sustainable livelihood for rural families through dairy farming. 

Eligibility criteria for the Micro Finance Scheme include being a resident of Gujarat. 

Applicants must be involved in dairy farming or be part of a registered self-help group. 

The age limit for applicants is set between 18 to 60 years. 

The income limit for eligibility is set at INR 1.5 lakh per annum for individuals and INR 2.5 lakh for families. 

To apply for the scheme, beneficiaries must fill out an application form available at GNDTDC offices or online. 

Required documents include proof of identity such as Aadhar card or voter ID. 

Applicants must also provide proof of residence and income certificates. 

Additionally, a recommendation letter from the local dairy cooperative society is required. 

Once the application is submitted, it undergoes a verification process by GNDTDC officials. 

After verification, eligible applicants are invited for an interview to discuss their dairy farming plans. 

Successful applicants receive a loan sanction letter detailing the loan amount and repayment terms. 

Disbursement of funds is typically done through bank transfers to the beneficiaries' accounts. 

The GNDTDC conducts regular monitoring and evaluation of the scheme's impact on beneficiaries. 

The scheme also encourages beneficiaries to maintain proper records of their dairy operations. 

Training programs are conducted periodically to educate beneficiaries on best practices in dairy farming. 

The GNDTDC collaborates with various banks to facilitate the loan disbursement process. 

The scheme has been instrumental in increasing milk production in the state of Gujarat. 

As of March 2023, over 15,000 beneficiaries have received financial assistance under this scheme. 

The total amount disbursed under the Micro Finance Scheme has exceeded INR 100 crores. 

The scheme has also contributed to the establishment of over 5,000 new dairy cooperatives. 

Beneficiaries report an increase in their monthly income by an average of 30 percent after availing of the scheme. 

The GNDTDC also provides support in marketing the dairy products produced by beneficiaries. 

The scheme has led to the creation of over 20,000 jobs in the dairy sector. 

Women beneficiaries have reported a significant improvement in their socio-economic status. 

The GNDTDC has also partnered with NGOs to enhance the outreach of the scheme. 

Regular workshops and seminars are organized to share success stories and best practices. 

The scheme is part of the larger initiative to promote the dairy sector in India. 

The Government of India has recognized the importance of dairy farming in rural development. 

The Micro Finance Scheme aligns with the National Dairy Plan launched in 2012. 

The GNDTDC aims to expand the scheme to include more beneficiaries in the coming years. 

The scheme also focuses on promoting organic dairy farming practices. 

Beneficiaries are encouraged to adopt sustainable practices to enhance productivity. 

The GNDTDC provides technical support to beneficiaries for improving milk quality. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries regarding its impact on their livelihoods. 

The GNDTDC is committed to ensuring transparency in the loan disbursement process. 

Regular audits are conducted to ensure proper utilization of funds. 

The scheme has been instrumental in reducing rural poverty in Gujarat. 

The GNDTDC continues to explore new avenues for funding and support for the scheme. 

The Micro Finance Scheme is a vital component of the government's efforts to boost the dairy sector. 

The scheme has been recognized as a model for similar initiatives in other states. 

The GNDTDC is dedicated to enhancing the overall development of the dairy industry in Gujarat. 

The scheme has successfully integrated technology into dairy farming practices. 

Beneficiaries are trained in using mobile applications for managing their dairy operations. 

The GNDTDC also provides assistance in obtaining necessary licenses and certifications for dairy products. 

The scheme has contributed to increasing the availability of quality milk in the market. 

The GNDTDC aims to create a robust support system for dairy farmers through this scheme. 

The Micro Finance Scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to rural development. 

The GNDTDC continues to monitor the changing needs of dairy farmers to adapt the scheme accordingly. 

The scheme has been a significant step towards achieving self-sufficiency in milk production in India. 

The GNDTDC encourages beneficiaries to participate in local fairs and exhibitions to promote their products. 

The scheme has fostered a sense of community among dairy farmers in Gujarat. 

The GNDTDC remains focused on empowering women through financial independence in dairy farming. 

The Micro Finance Scheme is a crucial initiative for sustainable rural development in India.
